points.point: Five essential elements of a valid contract; writing is the element specific to real estate sales
Statute of Frauds: an oral real estate sales contract isn't illegal, just unenforceable
Consideration: good and valuable consideration; courts don't weigh adequacy of price
Express (stated in words) vs. implied (created by conduct) contracts
Bilateral (promise for promise) vs. unilateral (promise for act, e.g. option)
Executory (still to be performed) vs. executed (fully performed)
Contract with a minor is voidable by the minor only
Contract by someone already adjudicated incompetent is void
Fraud and misrepresentation make a contract voidable by the victim
Duress (threats/force) vs. undue influence (abuse of trust/control)
Mutual mistake of material fact can void a contract; unilateral mistake or mistake of value/law usually doesn't
Puffing (vague opinion) is not misrepresentation
Signing for another requires authority, typically a power of attorney
Brokers fill in forms but don't give legal advice; refer legal questions to an attorney
Offeror/offeree and the ways an offer ends (acceptance, rejection, counteroffer, revocation, expiration, death/incompetence, destruction)
Offeror may revoke any time before acceptance is communicated, even if the offer promises to stay open
Acceptance must be unconditional and communicated (delivered) to the offeror or offeror's agent
A counteroffer rejects and kills the original offer
Multiple offers: present all promptly; seller decides; don't disclose one buyer's terms to another
Offers received after acceptance must still be presented; backup offers
E-SIGN and UETA give electronic signatures the same effect when parties agree to deal electronically
Option: optionee holds the right, optionor is bound; needs separate consideration; unilateral until exercised
Right of first refusal = right to match a third-party offer; no set price, owner can't be forced to sell
Assignment leaves the assignor liable; novation releases the original party
Personal services contracts (e.g. listings) can't be assigned without consent
Contingency = condition that must be met before a party must perform
Time is of the essence makes deadlines strict; missing one is a breach
Addendum (part of contract when signed) vs. amendment (later change, signed by all)
Specific performance: mainly a buyer's remedy because land is unique
Compensatory damages: money for the actual loss
Liquidated damages: earnest money as agreed damages; sole-remedy clause caps recovery
Rescission: cancel and restore parties (fraud, mutual mistake); acceptance of breach
Earnest money isn't required for validity; buyer's promise is consideration
Statute of limitations bars late claims
Discharge: full/substantial performance, mutual release, novation, impossibility, operation of law, breach
Purchase contract gives the buyer equitable title before closing
Estate for years has fixed dates and ends without notice; periodic tenancy needs notice
Tenancy at sufferance: holdover without landlord's consent
Sale of the property doesn't end an existing lease
Lease types: gross, net, triple net, ground, graduated, index
Percentage lease calculation (base rent + % of sales over threshold)
Lease option (may buy) vs. lease-purchase (agrees to buy)
Assignment of lease vs. sublease
Caveat emptor replaced; sellers and brokers must disclose known material defects, and concealment is fraud
Material fact = would affect a reasonable buyer's decision or price
Latent (hidden) vs. patent (visible) defects
Seller disclosure form: seller's actual knowledge, not a warranty, not a substitute for inspection
Stigmatized property; Colorado: homicide/felony/suicide/HIV not material facts (C.R.S. 38-35.5-101)
Recommend experts: home inspection, survey for boundary issues, specialized inspections
Red flags such as pipes from the ground (possible UST): disclose and recommend inspection
Lead-based paint (pre-1978): pamphlet, known info, warning statement, 10-day buyer inspection
Lead records kept 3 years
Lead rule for leases: disclosure applies, but tenants get no 10-day inspection right; exemptions
Radon: EPA action level 4 pCi/L
Asbestos: dangerous when friable; leave in place or encapsulate
Mold: fix the moisture source
UFFI and formaldehyde
Wetlands: Clean Water Act, Army Corps permit
CERCLA: strict, joint and several, retroactive liability for current owners
Phase I environmental site assessment supports CERCLA defenses
Special flood hazard areas: flood insurance required with federally backed/regulated loans
NFIP 30-day waiting period (loan exception); homeowners policies exclude flood
Statute of Frauds and the writing requirement
Bilateral vs. unilateral contracts
Executory vs. executed
Capacity: minors voidable, adjudicated incompetents void
Undue influence vs. duress
Puffing vs. misrepresentation
Acceptance must be communicated; revocation before delivery
Counteroffers kill the original offer
Presenting multiple offers
Electronic signatures under UETA/E-SIGN
Option vs. right of first refusal
Novation releases the original party; assignment doesn't
Time is of the essence
Addendum vs. amendment (with lead disclosure attachment)
Contingency termination by deadline avoids default and forfeiture of earnest money
Specific performance as the buyer's remedy
Liquidated damages / earnest money as sole remedy
Fraud/concealment makes contract voidable; rescission remedy
Tenancy at sufferance
Triple net lease
Percentage lease math
Sublease vs. assignment of lease
Lease option exercised becomes a bilateral contract
Duty to disclose known latent defects; latent vs. patent
Red flags and USTs: disclose and recommend experts
Lead-based paint disclosure and record keeping
Radon action level
Asbestos handling
CERCLA liability
Flood insurance requirement in SFHAs
